module_title: Basics of Motion: Distance, Displacement, and Acceleration
introduction: Kinematics is the branch of physics that describes the motion of points, bodies, and systems without considering the forces that cause them to move. First, we must understand the fundamental terms used to describe 'how' things move.

core_concepts.title: Rest and Motion are Relative
core_concepts.description: An object is in motion if it changes its position with respect to its surroundings over time. Motion is always relative. (e.g., A passenger in a moving train is at rest relative to the train, but in motion relative to the trees outside).

core_concepts.title: Distance vs. Displacement
core_concepts.description:
1. Distance (Scalar): The total actual path length covered by a moving body. It is always positive and can never be zero for a moving body.
2. Displacement (Vector): The shortest straight-line distance between the initial and final positions. It can be positive, negative, or zero.

core_concepts.title: Speed vs. Velocity
core_concepts.description:
1. Speed (Scalar): Distance traveled per unit time. (Speed = Distance / Time).
2. Velocity (Vector): Displacement per unit time. It is 'Speed with a specific direction'. (Velocity = Displacement / Time).

core_concepts.title: Acceleration
core_concepts.description: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity over time. If a car speeds up, changes direction, or slows down, it is accelerating. Its SI unit is m/s². Negative acceleration (slowing down) is called 'Retardation' or 'Deceleration'.

important_entities.name: Zero Displacement
important_entities.significance: If an athlete completes one full round of a circular track and returns to the exact starting line, the distance covered is the circumference (2πr), but the Displacement is ZERO.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Velocity can change even if Speed is constant
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: 'Can an object have constant speed but changing velocity?' YES. In 'Uniform Circular Motion', the speed remains constant, but because the direction is continuously changing at every point, the velocity is considered to be constantly changing.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember the initial letters. Distance pairs with Speed. Displacement pairs with Velocity.

exam_strategy_tips: A frequent conceptual question: 'What does the slope of a Distance-Time graph represent?' Answer: Speed. 'What does the slope of a Velocity-Time graph represent?' Answer: Acceleration.
